examples.en: These days AI is a big topic in the art world.

examples.ko: 예술계 사람들은 밤늦게까지 일하는 경우가 많아요.
examples.en: People in the art world often work until late at night.

examples.ko: 예술계 진출을 꿈꾸는 학생들이 정말 많아요.
examples.en: Lots of students dream of entering the art world.

examples.ko: 우리 삼촌은 예술계와 전혀 상관없는 일을 해요.
examples.en: My uncle does work that has nothing to do with the art world.
I heard funding for the arts will increase starting this year.
I heard the art world is really competitive.

explain: 음악, 미술, 무용 같은 예술 분야 사람들과 그 사회를 함께 가리켜요. 뉴스나 기사에서 '예술계 인사', '예술계 반응'처럼 자주 보여요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '예술 쪽'이라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It refers to the field of arts such as music, painting and dance together with the people in it. You often see it in news as '예술계 인사' or '예술계 반응'. In casual talk people also say '예술 쪽'.

examples.ko: 저쪽 자리는 예약석이라서 앉으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: That seat over there is reserved, so you can't sit there.

examples.ko: 식당에 가 보니 창가 자리가 모두 예약석이었어요.
examples.en: When I got to the restaurant, all the window seats were reserved.

examples.ko: 예약석 표지가 놓인 테이블은 비워 두세요.
examples.en: Please leave the tables with a reserved sign empty.

examples.ko: 공연장 앞쪽에 예약석이 따로 마련돼 있어요.
examples.en: There are reserved seats set aside at the front of the hall.

examples.ko: 예약석에 모르는 사람이 앉아 있어서 직원을 불렀어요.
examples.en: A stranger was sitting in my reserved seat, so I called a staff member.
Since it's a family gathering, I asked for a large reserved area.

explain: 식당, 공연장, 기차처럼 미리 자리를 잡아 둔 곳에 써요. 반대로 먼저 오는 사람이 앉는 자리는 '자유석'이라고 해요. 지하철의 '노약자석'은 예약석이 아니라 양보해야 하는 자리예요.
explain_en: It is used for seats held in advance at restaurants, concert halls or trains. The opposite, first-come seating, is called '자유석'. The '노약자석' on the subway is not a reserved seat but one you give up for people who need it.

examples.en: This hair salon operates entirely by appointment.
Most popular restaurants take reservations only.

examples.ko: 박물관이 예약제로 바뀌어서 미리 신청해야 해요.
examples.en: The museum switched to reservations only, so you have to sign up ahead.

examples.ko: 예약제라서 갑자기 가면 들어갈 수 없어요.
examples.en: It's by reservation only, so you can't get in if you just show up.

examples.ko: 병원은 예약제를 시작한 뒤로 대기 시간이 줄었어요.
examples.en: Since the clinic started taking appointments only, waiting times have gotten shorter.

examples.ko: 저 카페는 예약제가 아니니까 편하게 오세요.
examples.en: That café doesn't require reservations, so come whenever.

explain: 미리 예약한 사람만 받는 방식이에요. 미용실, 식당, 병원처럼 쓰고 '예약제로 운영하다', '예약제로 바뀌다'로 자주 말해요. 예약 없이 가는 방식은 '선착순'이나 '현장 접수'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a system that accepts only people who booked in advance. It is used for salons, restaurants and clinics, as in '예약제로 운영하다' and '예약제로 바뀌다'. Going without a booking is called '선착순' (first come, first served) or '현장 접수' (walk-in registration).

examples.en: Please tell me when the oven has finished preheating.

examples.ko: 겨울에는 차 예열을 잠깐 해 주는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: In winter it's good to let the car warm up for a moment.

examples.ko: 예열 시간이 너무 길어서 기다리기 힘들었어요.
examples.en: The preheating time was so long that it was hard to wait.

examples.ko: 이 레시피는 예열 없이 바로 구워도 돼요.
examples.en: You can bake this recipe right away without preheating.
Please set the preheating temperature to 180 degrees.

examples.ko: 고기를 굽기 전에 팬 예열부터 해요.
examples.en: Before grilling meat, I start by preheating the pan.

explain: 오븐, 팬, 엔진처럼 쓰기 전에 미리 데우는 일이에요. 요리 레시피에서 '오븐을 180도로 예열하세요'처럼 아주 자주 나와요. 경기나 행사 앞의 '몸풀기'를 비유로 말할 때도 있어요.
explain_en: It is warming something such as an oven, pan or engine before use. Recipes very often say '오븐을 180도로 예열하세요'. It can also be used figuratively for warming up before a game or event.

examples.ko: 빵을 굽기 전에 오븐을 먼저 예열해요.
examples.en: I preheat the oven before baking bread.

examples.ko: 팬을 충분히 예열한 다음에 기름을 두르세요.
examples.en: Heat the pan well first, and then add the oil.

examples.ko: 오븐을 예열하는 동안 반죽을 만들어 볼까요?
examples.en: Shall we make the dough while the oven preheats?
I forgot to preheat, so the cake came out undercooked.

examples.ko: 히터가 엔진을 예열해 줘서 시동이 잘 걸려요.
examples.en: The heater warms up the engine, so the car starts well.
Ten minutes of preheating is enough, so don't worry.

explain: 요리나 기계를 쓰기 전에 미리 데운다는 뜻으로 써요. 레시피에서 '예열해 두세요'처럼 자주 나와요. '데우다'는 식은 음식에도 쓰지만 '예열하다'는 오븐, 팬, 엔진처럼 쓰기 전 준비 단계에만 써요.
explain_en: It means to heat something ahead of use in cooking or machines. Recipes often say '예열해 두세요'. '데우다' also applies to reheating cold food, but '예열하다' is only for the preparation step before using an oven, pan or engine.

examples.en: The referee pulled out a yellow card for that player.
He committed a foul and got a yellow card.
Two yellow cards means you're sent off.

examples.ko: 우리 팀 수비수는 벌써 옐로카드 한 장을 받았어요.
examples.en: Our team's defender has already received one yellow card.

examples.ko: 옐로카드 때문에 다음 경기에 못 나온대요.
examples.en: I heard he can't play in the next match because of his yellow cards.

examples.ko: 오늘 경기는 옐로카드가 너무 많이 나왔어요.
examples.en: Too many yellow cards were shown in today's match.

explain: 축구에서 심판이 경고를 줄 때 보여 주는 카드예요. 한 경기에서 두 장을 받으면 '레드카드'로 퇴장당해요. 일상에서 '옐로카드를 받았다'고 하면 가벼운 경고를 받았다는 농담으로도 써요.
explain_en: It is the card a referee shows to give a warning in soccer. Two in one match leads to a '레드카드' and being sent off. In daily life, '옐로카드를 받았다' can also jokingly mean you got a mild warning.

examples.en: It's all in the past now, so let's forget it.
Grandmother sometimes smiles as she remembers the old days.
That kind of hardship has already become a thing of the past.
Please don't keep bringing up the past.

examples.ko: 동창들을 만나면 옛일 이야기로 밤을 새워요.
examples.en: When we meet our old classmates, we stay up all night talking about old times.
Our fight is already ancient history.

explain: '과거'보다 정감 있고 '지금은 지나간 일'이라는 느낌이 강해요. '옛일이 되다', '옛일을 떠올리다'처럼 자주 써요. '옛날 일'이라고 띄어 말해도 비슷해요.
explain_en: It feels warmer than '과거' and strongly suggests something that has passed. It is common in '옛일이 되다' and '옛일을 떠올리다'. Saying it as two words, '옛날 일', is nearly the same.

examples.en: On the first full moon of the year, we eat five-grain rice.

examples.ko: 어머니가 오곡밥과 나물을 한 상 차려 주셨어요.
examples.en: My mother laid out a table of five-grain rice and seasoned vegetables.
Five-grain rice is nutty because grains are mixed in with the rice.
This year I cooked five-grain rice myself.

examples.ko: 이웃집에서 오곡밥을 나눠 줘서 맛있게 먹었어요.
examples.en: The neighbors shared some five-grain rice, and we enjoyed it.

examples.ko: 마트에서 오곡밥 재료를 한 봉지에 팔아요.
examples.en: The supermarket sells five-grain rice ingredients in one bag.

explain: 쌀, 찹쌀, 수수, 팥, 콩 같은 여러 곡식을 섞어 지은 밥이에요. 정월 대보름에 먹는 음식으로 유명하고, 보통 나물 반찬과 함께 먹어요. 평소에는 '잡곡밥'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is rice cooked with several grains mixed in, such as glutinous rice, sorghum, red beans and soybeans. It is famous as a dish for the first full moon of the year and is usually eaten with seasoned vegetables. On ordinary days people also call mixed-grain rice '잡곡밥'.

examples.en: The plastic touched by the flame shrivelled up right away.
I washed the sweater in hot water and it shrank.
The leaves on the plant are drying out and curling up.

examples.ko: 추운 날에는 손가락이 오그라드는 것 같아요.
examples.en: On cold days it feels like my fingers are curling up.
Hearing that line makes me cringe.
When the air leaked out, the balloon slowly shrivelled.

explain: 열이나 추위, 마름 때문에 물건이 안쪽으로 쪼그라드는 모습에 써요. '줄어들다'는 크기가 작아지는 것이고, 이 말은 구겨지고 말리듯 오므라지는 모양이 핵심이에요. 요즘은 '손발이 오그라들다'로 민망한 느낌을 말하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.example: 옛날에 쓴 일기를 읽으니 손발이 오그라들어요.
phrases.en: Reading the diary I wrote long ago makes me cringe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 너무 민망하거나 낯간지러운 말이나 장면에 쓰는 말이에요. 실제 손발이 아니라 부끄러운 느낌을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for words or scenes that are embarrassingly cheesy or awkward. It describes a cringing feeling, not real hands and feet.

explain_en: It describes things pulling inward and shrivelling because of heat, cold or dryness. '줄어들다' just means getting smaller, while this word is about curling and puckering. These days it is often used in '손발이 오그라들다' to express cringing.

en: occasionally; by chance; once in a while

examples.en: Drop by whenever you're passing. You're always welcome.
I got to know that person just by running into them now and then.
When we run into each other, we greet each other warmly.
My brother and I do argue from time to time.

examples.ko: 오다가다 눈에 띄는 가게라서 한번 들어가 봤어요.
examples.en: It was a shop I kept noticing as I passed by, so I went in once.
I've seen the face around, but I don't know the name.

explain: '오고 가는 도중에'라는 뜻에서 나와, 특별한 약속 없이 우연히나 가끔 일어나는 일에 써요. '자주'보다는 가볍고 우연한 느낌이에요. '오다가다 만난 사이'는 깊지 않은 인연을 말할 때 많이 써요.
explain_en: It comes from 'on the way coming and going' and is used for things that happen by chance or now and then, without any plan. It feels lighter and more incidental than '자주'. '오다가다 만난 사이' is a common way to describe a casual acquaintance.

examples.en: The child pushed the tumbler doll and laughed out loud.
A tumbler doll stands right back up even if you knock it over.

examples.ko: 책상 위에 빨간 오뚝이 인형이 놓여 있어요.
examples.en: A red tumbler doll sits on the desk.
Grandfather bought a tumbler doll for his grandchild.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 오뚝이처럼 다시 일어나 우승했어요.
examples.en: That athlete bounced back like a tumbler doll and won.

examples.ko: 오뚝이 정신으로 다시 한번 도전해 볼게요.
examples.en: I'll try once more with a never-give-up spirit.

explain: 밑이 둥글고 무거워서 넘어뜨려도 다시 서는 전통 장난감이에요. 실패해도 포기하지 않고 다시 일어나는 사람을 비유할 때 자주 써요. 이때는 '오뚝이처럼 일어서다'로 말해요.

phrases.en: Even after his business failed, he bounced back.
phrases.nuance_ko: 넘어져도 포기하지 않고 다시 일어서는 끈기를 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise someone's resilience in getting back up after falling.

explain_en: It is a traditional toy with a round, weighted bottom that rights itself after being knocked over. It is often used as a metaphor for a person who gets back up after failure. In that sense you say '오뚝이처럼 일어서다'.

examples.en: The kids are running up and down the stairs.

examples.ko: 엘리베이터가 고장 나서 오르락내리락 걸어 다녔어요.
examples.en: The elevator broke, so I walked up and down the stairs.
The stock price moved up and down all day.
The boat rocked up and down on the waves.
My fever kept going up and down, so I went to the hospital.
I walked up and down the mountain path and my legs hurt.

explain: 위로 올라갔다 아래로 내려갔다를 되풀이하는 모습을 나타내요. 계단이나 산길뿐 아니라 가격, 체온, 기분처럼 변하는 것에도 써요. 보통 '오르락내리락하다'로 동사처럼 많이 써요.
explain_en: It shows something repeatedly going up and then down. It is used not only for stairs and mountain paths but also for things that fluctuate, like prices, body temperature and mood. It is also very often used as the verb '오르락내리락하다'.

examples.ko: 요즘 환율이 하루에도 몇 번씩 오르락내리락해요.
examples.en: These days the exchange rate goes up and down several times a day.
My grades keep going up and down, and I'm worried.
The baby's temperature went up and down all night.
There are days when my mood goes up and down.

examples.ko: 저 아이들은 왜 계단을 오르락내리락하고 있어요?
examples.en: Why are those kids going up and down the stairs?
When prices fluctuate, it's hard to keep a household ledger.

explain: 실제로 위아래로 움직이는 것과 값이나 상태가 변하는 것 모두에 써요. '변동하다'보다 구어적이고, 좋았다 나빴다 하는 불안정한 느낌이 있어요. '기분이 오르락내리락하다'는 감정 기복이 있다는 뜻으로 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It covers both physical up-and-down movement and values or conditions that keep changing. It is more colloquial than '변동하다' and has a feel of instability, good then bad. '기분이 오르락내리락하다' is a common way to say your moods swing.

examples.en: In winter a duck-down jacket is the warmest.

examples.ko: 이 이불은 오리털이 가득 들어 있어요.
examples.en: This blanket is stuffed full of duck down.

examples.ko: 오리털 패딩을 세탁할 때는 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: You have to be careful when washing a duck-down padded coat.
I bought a light, warm duck-down pillow.
Down feathers poked out and made the coat look messy.
Duck down is cheaper than goose down.

explain: 패딩이나 이불 속에 넣는 오리의 부드러운 털이에요. 비슷한 재료로 '거위털(구스다운)'이 있는데, 보통 더 비싸요. 옷 상표에서는 '다운'이라는 말도 같이 봐요.
explain_en: It is the soft down of ducks used to fill padded coats and blankets. A similar material is '거위털' (goose down), which is usually pricier. On clothing labels you will also see the word '다운'.

examples.ko: 여름에는 시원한 오이소박이가 입맛을 살려 줘요.
examples.en: In summer, cool stuffed cucumber kimchi brings back your appetite.
My mother is making stuffed cucumber kimchi.
Stuffed cucumber kimchi is made with a chive seasoning filling.
It's really tasty to have stuffed cucumber kimchi with noodles.
Stuffed cucumber kimchi came out as a side dish at the restaurant.

examples.ko: 오이소박이는 오래 두면 물러져서 빨리 먹어야 해요.
examples.en: Stuffed cucumber kimchi gets soft if left long, so you should eat it soon.

explain: 오이에 칼집을 내고 양념 속을 채워 만든 여름 김치예요. 일반 김치보다 오래 두기 어려워서 보통 담근 뒤 며칠 안에 먹어요. 줄여서 '소박이'라고 하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is a summer kimchi made by slitting a cucumber and stuffing it with seasoning. It does not keep as long as regular kimchi, so people usually eat it within a few days. It is sometimes shortened to '소박이'.

examples.en: The ozone layer blocks harmful ultraviolet rays.

examples.ko: 오존층이 얇아지면 피부암이 늘 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the ozone layer gets thinner, skin cancer can increase.

examples.ko: 과학 시간에 오존층 파괴에 대해 배웠어요.
examples.en: In science class we learned about the destruction of the ozone layer.
They say freon gas damages the ozone layer.
A hole has formed in the ozone layer above Antarctica.

examples.ko: 오존층 보호를 위해 사용을 줄이는 나라가 많아요.
examples.en: Many countries cut their use to protect the ozone layer.

explain: 지구 위 높은 곳에서 자외선을 막아 주는 층이에요. 환경 뉴스에서 '오존층 파괴', '오존층 보호'로 자주 나와요. 도시 공기 오염을 말하는 '오존 경보'와는 다른 이야기예요.
explain_en: It is the high layer above Earth that blocks ultraviolet rays. It often appears in environmental news as '오존층 파괴' and '오존층 보호'. It is a different topic from the '오존 경보' (ozone alert) about city air pollution.

examples.en: I have the chills, so maybe I caught a cold.

examples.ko: 열이 오르기 전에 심한 오한을 느꼈어요.
examples.en: I felt a severe chill before my fever rose.

examples.ko: 오한 때문에 이불을 두 겹이나 덮었어요.
examples.en: Because of the chills, I covered myself with two layers of blankets.

examples.ko: 몸살이 나면 오한과 근육통이 같이 와요.
examples.en: When you come down with body aches, chills and muscle pain come together.
If the chills continue, please go to the hospital.

examples.ko: 갑자기 오한이 들어서 일찍 집에 왔어요.
examples.en: I suddenly got the chills, so I came home early.

explain: 몸이 아플 때 으슬으슬 춥고 떨리는 느낌이에요. 보통 '오한이 나다', '오한이 들다'로 써요. 무서워서 소름 돋는 느낌은 '오싹하다'라고 하고, 이 말과 달라요.
explain_en: It is the shivery, cold feeling when your body is ill. It is usually used as '오한이 나다' or '오한이 들다'. The goosebump feeling from fear is '오싹하다', which is different.

examples.en: I lay down in the ondol room of the hanok and my back felt warm.

examples.ko: 이 펜션은 온돌방과 침대방이 따로 있어요.
examples.en: This pension has separate ondol rooms and bed rooms.
In winter an ondol room is the best.
The floor of the ondol room at Grandma's house is toasty hot.
If you book an ondol room, you sleep on bedding laid on the floor.

examples.ko: 외국인 친구들이 온돌방 체험을 해 보고 싶대요.
examples.en: My foreign friends say they want to try an ondol room.

explain: 바닥 아래로 따뜻한 열이 지나가게 만든 한국식 방이에요. 숙소에서는 침대 없이 바닥에 이불을 깔고 자는 방을 '온돌방'이라고 해요. 침대가 있는 방은 '침대방'이라고 구분해요.
explain_en: It is a Korean-style room where warmth passes under the floor. At lodgings, an '온돌방' is a room where you sleep on bedding laid on the floor with no bed. Rooms with beds are distinguished as '침대방'.

examples.en: At the bathhouse I got into the warm bath to loosen up.
I tried going back and forth between the hot and cold baths.

examples.ko: 온탕은 너무 뜨거워서 오래 못 있겠어요.
examples.en: The hot bath is so hot that I can't stay long.
The kids splashed around in the warm bath.

examples.ko: 피곤할 때는 온탕에 십 분쯤 몸을 담가요.
examples.en: When I'm tired, I soak in the warm bath for about ten minutes.

examples.ko: 이 사우나는 온탕이 두 개나 있어요.
examples.en: This sauna has as many as two hot baths.

explain: 대중목욕탕에서 따뜻한 물이 있는 탕을 말해요. 반대말은 '냉탕'이고, 보통 두 탕을 번갈아 이용해요. 집 욕조의 따뜻한 물에는 잘 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It refers to the pool with warm water in a public bathhouse. The opposite is '냉탕', and people often alternate between the two. It is not typically used for warm water in a home bathtub.

examples.en: With the fan heater on in the office, it's warm.
My throat is dry because of the fan heater's air.

examples.ko: 교실 온풍기가 고장 나서 모두 외투를 입고 있어요.
examples.en: The classroom heater broke, so everyone is wearing coats.
I sat next to the heater and now I'm sleepy.

examples.ko: 작은 온풍기를 하나 사서 발밑에 두었어요.
examples.en: I bought a small fan heater and put it under my feet.
Fan heaters use a lot of electricity, so be careful.

explain: 더운 바람을 내보내서 공간을 데우는 난방 기구예요. 겨울철 사무실이나 교실에서 흔하고, 바닥을 데우는 '온돌'이나 '보일러'와는 방식이 달라요. 에어컨의 난방 기능을 말할 때는 '온풍'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is a heater that warms a space by blowing hot air. It is common in offices and classrooms in winter and works differently from floor heating ('온돌') or a '보일러'. The heating mode of an air conditioner is also called '온풍'.

en: how good one looks in clothes; the look of an outfit

examples.en: That friend looks really good in clothes.

examples.ko: 키가 커서 뭘 입어도 옷맵시가 나요.
examples.en: She's tall, so she looks good in whatever she wears.
To make the outfit look better, define the waistline.
Grandmother is known for how graceful she looks in a hanbok.

examples.ko: 이 코트는 옷맵시가 안 나서 반품했어요.
examples.en: This coat didn't hang well, so I returned it.
When it comes to how well they wear clothes, they're the best in our class.

explain: 옷을 입었을 때 모양이 얼마나 보기 좋은지를 말해요. '옷맵시가 나다', '옷맵시가 좋다'로 자주 써요. 옷 자체가 아니라 입은 모습의 느낌이라서 '옷태'나 '핏'과 비슷하게 말해요.
explain_en: It refers to how good you look when wearing clothes. It is common as '옷맵시가 나다' or '옷맵시가 좋다'. It is about the look of the outfit on the person rather than the clothes themselves, similar to '옷태' or '핏'.

examples.en: The baby has started babbling lately.
The babbling has increased, and the baby chatters all day.

examples.ko: 엄마가 말을 걸면 아기가 옹알이로 대답해요.
examples.en: When Mom talks to the baby, it answers with babbling.

examples.ko: 옹알이 소리가 너무 귀여워서 녹음해 두었어요.
examples.en: The babbling sounds so cute that I recorded it.

examples.ko: 우리 조카는 옹알이를 하다가 잠이 들었어요.
examples.en: My nephew fell asleep while babbling.

examples.ko: 옹알이는 보통 생후 몇 달부터 나타나요.
examples.en: Babbling usually appears a few months after birth.

explain: 말을 배우기 전의 아기가 내는 '아', '우' 같은 소리예요. 보통 '옹알이를 하다', '옹알이가 늘다'처럼 써요. 뜻 있는 첫 말을 하기 전 단계라서 육아 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is the 'ah' and 'oo' sounds a baby makes before learning to talk. It is typically used as '옹알이를 하다' or '옹알이가 늘다'. It comes up often in parenting talk as the stage before a baby's first real words.

examples.ko: 책을 읽다가 마음에 와닿는 문장을 적어 두었어요.
examples.en: While reading, I wrote down a sentence that struck a chord with me.

examples.ko: 비 오는 밤에는 노래 가사가 더 가슴에 와닿아요.
examples.en: On rainy nights, song lyrics hit home even more.
Only now did the teacher's advice really sink in.
If I only hear it in numbers, it doesn't really register.

examples.ko: 그 영화의 마지막 대사가 유난히 마음에 와닿았어요.
examples.en: The last line of that movie especially touched me.

examples.ko: 직접 겪어 보니 그 말이 확 와닿네요.
examples.en: Now that I've experienced it myself, those words really hit me.

explain: 어떤 말이나 이야기가 머리로만이 아니라 마음으로 느껴질 때 써요. '와 닿다'로 띄어 쓰지 않고 붙여서 써요. 부정형 '와닿지 않아요'는 '실감이 안 나요'와 비슷하게 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is used when words or stories are felt in the heart, not just understood in the head. It is written as one word, not '와 닿다'. The negative '와닿지 않아요' is often used much like '실감이 안 나요' (it doesn't feel real).

examples.en: When it started raining, I turned on the wipers.

examples.ko: 와이퍼가 낡아서 앞이 잘 안 보여요.
examples.en: The wipers are worn out, so I can't see ahead well.

examples.ko: 주차 위반 딱지가 와이퍼에 끼워져 있었어요.
examples.en: A parking ticket was tucked under the wiper.
At the shop I replaced the wiper blade rubber with a new one.
Please turn the wiper speed up to fast.

examples.ko: 겨울에는 와이퍼가 얼어붙지 않게 세워 두기도 해요.
examples.en: In winter, people sometimes lift the wipers so they don't freeze to the glass.

explain: 자동차 앞유리의 물기를 닦아 주는 장치예요. 일상에서는 '와이퍼' 그대로 쓰고, 차를 점검할 때 '와이퍼 날'이나 '와이퍼 고무'를 갈아 달라고 말해요. 영어 wiper처럼 다른 닦는 도구 전체를 뜻하지는 않아요.
explain_en: It is the device that wipes water off a car's windshield. In daily life people just say '와이퍼', and at a repair shop they ask to replace the '와이퍼 날' or '와이퍼 고무'. Unlike the English word, it doesn't refer to wiping tools in general.

examples.en: This furniture is delivered fully assembled.

examples.ko: 조립 키트보다 완성품이 값이 더 비싸요.
examples.en: The finished product costs more than the assembly kit.
At the factory they pick out and inspect only the finished goods.

examples.ko: 아직 완성품이 나오지 않아서 기다리는 중이에요.
examples.en: The finished product hasn't come out yet, so I'm waiting.
Seeing the finished product, it looked much better than the blueprint.

examples.ko: 완성품은 한 달 뒤에 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can receive the finished product in a month.

explain: 부품이나 재료 상태가 아니라 다 만들어져서 바로 쓸 수 있는 물건을 말해요. 반대 느낌의 말로는 '반제품'이나 '조립 제품'이 있어요. 장난감, 가구, 프라모델 같은 물건을 살 때 자주 구별해요.
explain_en: It refers to a thing that is completely made and ready to use, not in parts or materials. Contrasting words include '반제품' (semi-finished goods) and assemble-it-yourself products. The distinction often matters when buying toys, furniture or model kits.

examples.en: I use coarse salt when salting napa cabbage.

examples.ko: 고기를 구울 때 왕소금을 살짝 뿌렸어요.
examples.en: I sprinkled a little coarse salt when grilling the meat.

examples.ko: 왕소금은 알갱이가 굵어서 잘 녹지 않아요.
examples.en: Coarse salt has big grains, so it doesn't dissolve easily.
I bought a sack of coarse salt at the market.

examples.ko: 왕소금이 없으면 굵은 소금으로 대신해도 돼요.
examples.en: If you don't have coarse salt, you can substitute big-grain salt.
Around kimchi-making season, the price of coarse salt tends to rise.

explain: 알갱이가 굵은 소금이에요. 보통은 '굵은소금'이라고 더 많이 말하고, '왕소금'은 김장 때 배추를 절이는 큰 알갱이 소금을 가리키는 느낌이 있어요. 간을 맞추는 곱고 흰 소금은 '꽃소금'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is salt with large grains. People more often say '굵은소금', and '왕소금' has a feel of the big-grain salt used to brine cabbage for kimchi. The fine white salt for seasoning is '꽃소금'.

en: foreign-made product; being of foreign origin

examples.en: This fruit is imported, so it's cheap.

examples.ko: 식당 메뉴판에 고기가 외국산인지 국산인지 적혀 있어요.
examples.en: The restaurant menu says whether the meat is imported or domestic.
Many imported products have entered the market.

examples.ko: 저는 외국산보다 국산 채소를 더 자주 사요.
examples.en: I buy domestic vegetables more often than imported ones.
The packaging said 'foreign-made' in big letters.

examples.ko: 외국산 자동차를 타는 사람이 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: More people are driving foreign-made cars.

explain: 다른 나라에서 만들어지거나 자란 것을 말해요. 반대말은 '국산'이고, 식당이나 마트에서 원산지를 표시할 때 많이 보여요. 사람이 외국에서 왔다는 말에는 쓰지 않고, 물건과 농수산물에 써요.
explain_en: It refers to goods made or grown in another country. The opposite is '국산', and you see both in origin labels at restaurants and supermarkets. It is for products and farm or sea produce, never for people from abroad.
